title: Scanning tools: Nessus, OpenVAS, Qualys and Trivy

videos.script: A team bought a network scanner. It scans every server once a month, and the report is long. {{report}} Another team runs a scanner in its pipeline, on every image. Each team thinks the other one is wasting its time. Both are wrong. {{two}} The two tools stand in different places. One reads files before they run. The other knocks on the doors of what is already running. {{vantage}} In this lesson you look at linkbox from both places. From outside, it says it is gunicorn, and nothing more. From inside, every version is written down in a file. {{inside}} You will see what Nessus, OpenVAS and Qualys do, from their documentation, and why a scan that logs in finds more. Then you run Trivy for real, through five different doors: your image, your repository and your cluster. {{trivy}} By the end, you can start from a question and pick the tool that answers it. And you will know the rule that comes before any scan. Only what you own, or what somebody has allowed you, in writing, to scan. {{rule}}
